text: Update to the St. Johns River flood warning near Cocoa in Brevard County: rain water is still draining into the river. The river near Cocoa is expected to crest at major flood stage on Friday, higher than the crest after Hurricane Ian, and to stay flooded to some degree for weeks. Do not drive around barricades or through flooded areas, and use caution near the riverbanks.

The flood warning for the St. Johns River near Cocoa in Brevard County is still in effect. At 7:15 PM Thursday the river stood at 16.9 feet, which is above the 16.0-foot flood stage and in moderate flood stage. NWS expects it to reach major flood stage late this week and stay there through the weekend and into early next week. Do not drive around barricades or through flooded roads near the river.

agency: National Weather Service Melbourne (as reported by Florida Today)
text: The St. Johns River near Cocoa is expected to reach major flood stage. The Providence Road area west of Cocoa could become impassable and cut off access to the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Water could also flood low-lying areas near the river, including Lake Poinsett west of Cocoa, the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park area of Cocoa. Do not drive through flooded roads near the river.
